title: Spec mixes two incompatible tick conventions: u/s vs u/tick conversions contradict each other within the same document
evidence:
| Residential node throughput | 5 u/s (= 0.167 pkts/tick) | `data/node_types.json` |
| Era-3 demand | email 4/tick + streaming 2/tick = 6 arrivals/tick = 180 u/s | `data/demand.json` |
1 u = the transit work of one 1500-byte frame crossing one hop. At 20 Hz logic:
| 1 G (FTTH drop) | 83,333 pps | **4,167** |
detail: §2 derives u/tick by dividing pps by 20 (20 Hz), but §1/Thread 2 derive pkts/tick from u/s by dividing by 30 only. 6 arrivals/tick becomes '180 u/s' (×30) yet 6 pkts/tick becomes 1.4 Mbps (×20) — irreconcilable conventions.
recommended_fix: Declare one tick↔second↔unit convention; recompute 0.167/0.2/2.67 pkts/tick, the '180 u/s' line, and the ~1,000× compression from it.
